To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the feature learning approach is better than the end-to-end one, (2) the feature learning model is not necessarily deep, and (3) the feature learning and back-end classification are not necessarily jointly trained.

(a) the end-to-end learning approach is not always better than the feature learning approach for speaker verification, (b) feature learning approach out-performs the end-to-end one on the task of speaker verification, and (c) the end-toend approach is more robust than the feature learning one to the mismatch between training and testing data.
the feature learning outperforms the end-to-end learning approach in the deep SV, at least when the data and computational resources are similar to ours.

the following questions. (1) Can we learn a good speaker verification system end-to-end? (2) If we cannot, is there a way to improve it? and (3) If we can, what is the advantage of the end-to-end learning approach?
the following two questions: (1) Do we need end-to-end for deep speaker verification? and (2) What are the advantages of end-to-end?
a practical question: do we need end to-end?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
end-to-end learning is not a silver bullet in SV.
, in order to achieve the best performance, the end-to-end SV system should be trained with a very large amount of data and a powerful deep neural network, and it should be carefully fine-tuned.
, for the text-independent SV task, the feature learning approach is more effective than the end-to-end one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the feature learning is more robust and reliable than the end-to-end learning, which may be a good choice for the development of practical speaker verification systems.
, in the current state-of-the-art SV systems, the feature learning approach is still the best choice.
the end-to-end learning approach has not reached its potential in the SV task, at least with the current deep neural network architectures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the end-to-end SV approach is not necessarily the best choice.
the feature learning is a better choice for the current deep SV research.
we need to carefully design the end-to-end model and train it properly, and we need to carefully select and tune the feature learning and back-end classifier.
